thread:
tara: Heads up, CI started complaining in pyright about some generated client signatures. Looks like streaming endpoints are typed as `Iterator[...]` even though the SDK method is async.

nate: oh that's bad. Can you paste the generated client signature?

tara: sure:```python
class ConversationsClient:
    async def stream_messages(self, conv_id: str) -> Iterator[str]:
        resp = await self._raw_stream_request(conv_id)
        for chunk in resp:
            yield chunk.text
```

tara: pyright error: "Type of 'stream_messages' is incompatible with supertype 'Protocol' (reportIncompatibleMethodOverride)" because callers expect AsyncIterator[str].

lucy: generator template bug again? We probably render sync generator return type when the endpoint has `stream: true` but the generator doesn't detect `async_client` flag.

patrick: also got a flaky report: some downstream users on py3.9 hit `from __future__ import annotations` absence and forward refs in types caused `typing.Optional[Foo]` to render oddly. Might be related.

nate: two separate fixes: 1) streaming endpoints should produce `AsyncIterator[T]` when client is async. 2) add `from __future__ import annotations` at top of generated modules to avoid runtime forward-ref churn and make mypy/pyright happier.

lucy: I can whip up a small unit test that synthesizes an async client config and checks generated signature text includes `AsyncIterator`. That should catch regressions.

tara: note: we also saw generated types like `list[str]` which fails under py3.8 used by some CI runners. The generator assumes py3.9+. We should either pin minimum py version in SDK or fall back to `List[str]` from typing.

patrick: historically we wanted to support py3.8 for enterprise customers. Proposal: generator accepts `target_python_version` flag and toggles new syntax vs typing.List. We already do that for `Literal`/`typing_extensions`, so reuse pattern.

nate: good. For the async iterator fix, simplest patch in jinja:```jinja
{%- if client.is_async and prop.is_stream -%}
def {{name}}(...) -> AsyncIterator[{{item_type}}]:
{%- endif -%}
```

nate: Also need to ensure we import `from typing import AsyncIterator` (or typing_extensions for py3.8).

lucy: about `from __future__ import annotations` — adding it is safe for py>=3.7 and cleans up a lot. I'm +1.

tara: CI bot ran quick pyright job on our draft branch and still found one remaining codegen file where the return annotation was `typing.Iterable[str]` instead of `AsyncIterable[str]`. Looks like an edge case for server-sent events endpoints that were modeled as iterable streams in the spec.

ci-bot: pyright-check: 12 files flagged. 1 file uses Iterable vs AsyncIterable, 3 files use list[] literal on target_py=3.8, 8 files missing future annotations.

patrick: thanks bot. I'll sweep the generator. Question: do we try to be clever and convert `Iterable`->`AsyncIterable` only when method is `async def`? Or tie it to client.is_async flag?

nate: tie to async client flag. Some sync clients legitimately return Iterable. The spec alone doesn't imply sync vs async. The CLI generator knows the client runtime mode.

lucy: bumped a patch branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3502 includes: add future annotations, switch stream return types for async clients, add typing imports guarded by target_python_version, and tests for pyright + mypy.

tara: awesome. Can we also add a short CONTRIBUTING note explaining target_python_version and how to run pyright locally? New contributors keep forgetting to run the typing checks before pushing.

patrick: will add docs. Also add a lint rule in CI to fail if generated code contains `list[` when target is 3.8.

ci-bot: quick-run on patch branch: pyright errors reduced to 0 on changed files, full CI pending.

nate: once this lands, we should push a micro release to our internal SDK registry because the change affects streaming API surface and could be a breaking type change (sync -> async signatures fixed). Need to note it in changelog.

tara: agree. For the release, mark as non-breaking runtime but typing-only fix; still bump minor version and add migration note.

lucy: merging after a second reviewer. Thanks all. :rocket:
